h1: Why Static Forms Are Failing Modern Product Teams
p: Static surveys limit user insights by forcing rigid paths - discover why conversational AI is the future of user research.

For years, product teams have relied on static forms to gather user feedback. The process is always the same: write a list of questions, define the multiple-choice options, and hope users don't drop off before hitting submit.
The biggest flaw in this model is that it entirely misses the context behind a user's choice. If a user selects "Pricing" as their reason for churning, a static form stops there.
"We were collecting thousands of data points, but we still didn't understand our users' actual motivations. The data was wide, but incredibly shallow."
By replacing rigid surveys with dynamic AI interviews, teams can adapt to every user in real time.
It’s time to stop treating users like data points and start having real conversations with them.

/blog/how-to-craft-the-perfect-objective.title: How to Craft the Perfect Objective for Your AI Interviewer
/blog/how-to-craft-the-perfect-objective.description: Learn how to write clear research goals that help Ordara generate the most effective conversational surveys.
h1: How to Craft the Perfect Objective for Your AI Interviewer
p: Learn how to write clear research goals that help Ordara generate the most effective conversational surveys.
When launching a survey with Ordara, the AI builds its conversational strategy around the objective you set. The quality of your insight directly correlates to the clarity of your initial prompt.
A vague prompt like "Ask users about our app" will yield generic follow-ups. Instead, you need to be specific.
"A well-defined research objective acts as the north star for your AI interviewer, keeping the conversation on track even when users go on tangents."
Are you looking at onboarding friction, feature usability, or pricing clarity? Pick one primary focus per survey.
Tell the AI what not to focus on. For example, "Focus on the checkout experience, but ignore questions about shipping times."
Match the research style to the goal. An exploratory tone works best for new feature discovery, while a direct, analytical tone might be better for bug reporting.
